To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Andrew Li <andrew.li@prodlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: brief runway + canary schedule for Harbor9B onboarding (freeze window ask)

Team —

We received Prodlytics' signed SOW for Harbor9B and they want us live in hosted in ~2 weeks. Before we move forward I need a short internal freeze window for any runtime/model changes tied to this intake so we don’t overlap other rollouts. Summary ask:

- 72-hour model-change freeze window starting 2027-06-03 00:00 UTC (requesting a firm runway to run canaries and infra validation).
- Canary schedule: 3 stages (internal dry run -> 24h limited external canary -> 72h broad canary).
- Required deliverables: performance baseline, tokenizer compatibility note, OOM/latency thresholds for automatic rollback, telemetry dashboard link, and owner for customer notifications.

Attachments: harbor9b-integration-checklist.xlsx, canary-runbook.md (draft).

Why this is slightly different: Harbor9B uses a new tokenizer bundle and a moderate KV-cache format tweak; we want to avoid a surprise breaking change for existing customers during the onboarding window.

Andrew — looping you to confirm Prodlytics is okay with these phases and the proposed freeze window.

Next steps: can each team confirm feasibility by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference

---
Note: attachments are referenced; see harbor9b-integration-checklist.xlsx for checklist details.

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear ask. A few clarifying questions from infra/serving runtime perspective before I can commit to the 72-hour freeze:

1) QPS / peak concurrency expected during the canary and production after GA? We need numbers to estimate reserved pool sizing.
2) Memory/CPU footprint and whether the vendor will provide a quantized float16 or int8 variant.
3) Does Harbor9B require a tokenizer binary we don’t already ship, or are we using the tokenizer bundle in the checklist?

Notes: our standard lead time for reserved capacity adjustments is ~48 hours if we’re only changing autoscaler targets; anything that requires new GPU families or kernel changes needs 5 business days. If Harbor9B needs a new kernel path (e.g., different KV cache layout), we should schedule that separately.

Dev — can you confirm the kernel/kv cache compatibility callouts? Jonas — can you weigh in on tracing/telemetry hooks for the canary?

Karthik
Director, Inference Engineering
Redwood Inference

Marissa / team —

Quick compatibility and perf notes after an initial test on staging:

- Baseline (staging, seq=512): p50 token latency ~18ms, p95 ~72ms, cold-start latency for new worker ~220ms.
- Memory: typical serving footprint ~18.5GB for 8k KV cache active; quantized int8 variant reduces peak to ~10.2GB (recommended for hosted).
- Tokenizer: Harbor9B uses tokenizer v2 (differs from our default v1), requires a small vendor binary and token mapping table; does not block serving but must be shipped in the model bundle. That means a brief packaging step and a signed artifact from the vendor.
- KV cache: minor layout change (order of segment metadata) — backward-incompatible with legacy warm-start snapshots; we'll need to ensure canary workers start cold or use a migration path.

Suggested canary triggers (automatic rollback if any hit during canary window):
- latency_p95 > 250ms for 15m
- OOM rate > 0.5% of requests over 1h
- error rate spike > 1% above baseline for 30m

I attached canary-runbook.md (in the thread attachments) which includes run commands and a brief rollback playbook.

Procurement note: because of tokenizer v2 we may need a signed tokenizer artifact from a third-party; that could touch legal/compliance and might require a short procurement exception. Partners (cloudvendor) may also need to approve if the artifact runs on their managed packaging flow.

I can land the kernel-path checks and the packaging steps within 48 hours once we confirm the frozen window.

—Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Marissa / all —

OK — I approve a controlled freeze window but want to tighten the initial canary cadence:

- Approve a 48-hour runway for infra changes, with a constrained first canary of 24h limited to <1% of traffic (to Prodlytics users only). If that looks good, proceed to a wider 72h canary at 10% traffic.
- Rollback triggers should include Dev's suggested thresholds + an additional business-safety trigger: any customer-facing regression flagged by CS within the first 2h should trigger an immediate halt.
- Procurement: Marissa, please open the tokenizer exception ticket and loop Legal; if the vendor-signed tokenizer is required we will fast-track approval but need the artifact and license terms before the freeze starts.

Marissa — can you coordinate announcement to Sales/CS and confirm Andrew that Prodlytics is OK with the two-step canary timing? Andrew, appreciate confirmation on the 24h limited canary and approval to start on 2027-06-03 as proposed.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
